Apply for your key · Brief · API docs · Starter kit · Build page · Results · Discord

You are the procurement team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional German pump maker, and the inbox is full: a foundry wants +9.5 %, a framework contract expires, a new pump needs three quotes. Build an **AI buyer agent** that reads the company's data, negotiates by e-mail with our supplier bots, and closes the best total deal, or walks away. Practise all weekend against our hosted suppliers. On Sunday at 12:00 a Live Final on hidden cases ranks every team. This repo holds everything you need: the brief, the API docs, a Python starter kit and the data package. Bring your own LLM, any provider; we run the suppliers. ## Start in 15 minutes You need Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and git. 1. **Apply.** Open **https://arena.tacto.ai/apply** and enter your team name and a contact e-mail. Tip: start the name with one emoji, it shows on the big screen. 2. **Show your match code at the Tacto desk.** We approve. 3. **Copy your key.** It appears **once** on the page you applied on; then press "Got the key". One key per team. Lost it? We reset it at the desk. 4. **Run the four commands.** ```bash git clone https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit.git cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit cp .env.example .env # paste your key: ARENA_API_KEY=... uv sync --all-extras # install uv run arena me # your team and its practice quota uv run arena play case:P01 # the naive example agent negotiates one practice case uv run arena board # your team on the practice leaderboard ``` `arena play` prints the deal, your score and a replay link: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words. Read it, improve your agent, play again. Next steps, the LLM agent and your own agent: [starter-kit/README.md](starter-kit/README.md). ## Links | What | Where | |---|---| | Apply for your key | https://arena.tacto.ai/apply | | Brief: story, task, score, rules | [brief/brief.md](brief/brief.md) | | API docs | [brief/api.md](brief/api.md) | | Starter kit: client, example agents, Live Final runner, local simulator, MCP server | [starter-kit/](starter-kit/) | | Submission and pitch | [brief/submission.md](brief/submission.md) | | Practice build page: every team's quota, records and highlights | https://arena.tacto.ai/live | | Live Final results, team by team and case by case | https://arena.tacto.ai/results | | Questions | Discord https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV · the Tacto table | ## The weekend at a glance | When | What | |---|---| | Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit and practice arena go live | | Sat 12:00-13:00 | **Deep dive**, ground floor (room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A. Bring a laptop. Challenge selection closes 13:00 | | Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table. Practice all weekend: 200 sessions per team per 24 hours | | Sat evening | We post on Discord when Tacto goes offline for the night | | Sun 08:00 | **New market data.** Run `uv run arena data` again; hidden cases may cite it | | Sun 09:00 | Pre-flight: one practice case through your final setup | | Sun 12:00 | **Code freeze**, submit on ehl.gg. **Live Final**: five waves, 8 minutes each, every team at once | | Sun 13:00 | **Top 10 pitch** to the Tacto jury: 5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions | | Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced | | Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) | | Sun 16:30 | Awards | ## Rules that matter - **No human in the loop** during the Live Final. Start your agent before 12:00 and leave it running: `uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10` picks up each wave by itself. - **Your agent must not read the live feed** during the Live Final: `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`, `/results` and their JSON. They are for you, not for your agent. - **One key per team.** No attacks on the service or on other teams. - Everything else counts, including weaknesses you find in our suppliers. Every replay is open to the jury. All rules: [brief, section 7](brief/brief.md#7-rules). ## What to submit on ehl.gg by Sun 12:00 - **Your repo** with the agent and a README that says how to run it, and the **commit hash** your agent runs in the final. The jury and tum.ai must be able to open it. - **A short description** of your approach. - **Slides** for the pitch. The top 10 pitch from 13:00. Details: [brief/submission.md](brief/submission.md). ## Prizes 1st place €1,500 · medals for the top 3 · the best 2 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final. ⟦Q2: how the Live Final score and the jury combine for places 1-3⟧ ## What is in this repo | Folder | What | |---|---| | [`brief/`](brief/) | The brief, the API docs, the submission guide | | [`starter-kit/`](starter-kit/) | Python client, a naive and an LLM example agent, the Live Final runner, `arena-sim` (the API on your laptop), an MCP server over the data | | [`data/`](data/) | Data package v1: CSV, SQLite, `facts.json`, contracts, letters, notes. The same as `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`; start with [`data/README.md`](data/README.md) | The company, its suppliers and all names are fictional; the market indices are real open series ([`data/ATTRIBUTION.md`](data/ATTRIBUTION.md)). ## Licence Code: MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Data and docs: CC BY 4.0 ([LICENSE-data](LICENSE-data)). Your code is yours.

Read the brief first (`../brief/brief.md`); the full API is in `../brief/api.md`. Code: MIT. ## Quickstart - first agent on the board in 15 minutes You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). **1. Get your team's key** (one per team): open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail, and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once an organiser approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page (or its link) shows it; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it. Keep it out of git. ```bash cd starter-kit uv sync --all-extras # 2. install cp .env.example .env # 3. put ARENA_URL and your key (ARENA_API_KEY) into .env uv run arena me # 4. your team and its practice quota uv run arena cases # 5. the practice cases (the 10 hosted ones are playable) uv run arena play case:P01 -v # 6. the naive agent negotiates one case uv run arena board # 7. you are on the practice leaderboard ``` Is the arena up? `curl $ARENA_URL/health`. Step 6 prints the deal, your total cost `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the case score, and a **replay link**: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move, in words. That is the learning loop - play a practice case, read the replay, improve your agent, play again. In practice your best score per case counts, so play a case again whenever your agent improves. **Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours. `arena play` and `arena run` print how many are left; `arena run` plays only the hosted practice cases and stops starting new ones once the quota is used up (a `429` there does not go away by retrying). Plan your runs. **Now the LLM agent.** Download the data (`ARENA_DATA=data/package` in `.env`), choose a model in `.env` (your own key), then: ```bash uv run arena data # unpacks data/package (and the Sunday release once public) uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8 # every hosted practice case, 8 at a time uv run arena play case:D02 -v # the sandbox: 3 demo suppliers, no board ``` **Sunday 08:00:** run `arena data` again - it adds `data/release-sunday` (new news, letters, a memo). `DataPackage` merges its facts and documents automatically; hidden cases may cite them. ## Hello World (local, 3 commands) No key yet? Play a whole case against the local simulator - no network, no quota, no LLM costs. The simulator's supplier is a plain script; the real ones are on arena.tacto.ai. After `uv sync --all-extras` (step 2 above): ```bash # terminal 1: the simulator (--data is optional: leave it out until you have run `arena data`) uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package # terminal 2: a simulator key, then the naive agent plays case:S01 ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Hello World" sim # prints an api_key ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ARENA_API_KEY= uv run arena play case:S01 -v ``` It prints the deal, `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the score and a replay link - open it in your browser: the result on top, then every e-mail of the negotiation. ## Try it by hand (Postman, curl) Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the 60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock: ```bash uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim # prints a simulator api_key export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY= ``` Every call sends `X-API-Key: `; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a # Copy to .env (never commit it). Real environment variables win over this file. ARENA_URL=https://arena.tacto.ai # Your team's key from https://arena.tacto.ai/apply (one per team; never commit it) ARENA_API_KEY= # The unpacked data package (`arena data` puts it here; for the LLM agent and the MCP server) ARENA_DATA=data/package # LLM for the example agent - your own key. Either Anthropic ... LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic LLM_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5 LLM_EFFORT=low ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= # ... or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, a local Ollama, ...) # LLM_PROVIDER=openai # LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 # LLM_MODEL= # LLM_API_KEY= [project] name = "arena-kit" version = "0.1.0" description = "Starter kit for the Tacto Negotiation Arena: API client, example buyer agents, contract simulator, MCP server over the data package" readme = "README.md" requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13" dependencies = ["httpx>=0.27", "openpyxl>=3.1", "pypdf>=5"] [project.optional-dependencies] anthropic = ["anthropic>=1.0"] mcp = ["mcp>=2.3,<3"] sim = ["fastapi>=0.115", "uvicorn>=0.30"] [project.scripts] arena = "arena_kit.cli:main" arena-sim = "arena_kit.sim:main" [dependency-groups] dev = ["pytest>=8", "ruff>=0.6"] [build-system] requires = ["hatchling"] build-backend = "hatchling.build" [tool.ruff] line-length = 120 target-version = "py312" [tool.ruff.lint] select = ["E", "F", "I", "B", "UP"]

**Dein Teil**
Den Key hast du nur auf der Apply-Seite, deshalb trägst du ihn selbst in [`.env`](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/.env) ein:

```
ARENA_API_KEY=<dein key>
```

Für den LLM-Agent brauchst du außerdem `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` (oder `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` mit eigenem Endpoint). Das Modell steht schon auf `claude-opus-5-5` mit `LLM_EFFORT=low`.

**Danach**
```bash
cd /Users/jonathandemir/projects/tacto-challenge/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
uv run arena me
uv run arena play case:P01 -v
```

Sag mir Bescheid, sobald der Key drin ist, dann spiele ich den ersten Case durch und gehe mit dir das Replay und die Brief-Dokumente an. Am Sonntag um 08:00 (Release 06:00 UTC) einmal `uv run arena data` wiederholen.

## main...origin/main

60	# terminal 2: a simulator key, then the naive agent plays case:S01
61	ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Hello World" sim                  # prints an api_key
62	ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ARENA_API_KEY=<the api_key> uv run arena play case:S01 -v
63	```
64	
65	It prints the deal, `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the score and a replay link - open it
66	in your browser: the result on top, then every e-mail of the negotiation.
67	
68	## Try it by hand (Postman, curl)
69	
70	Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the
71	60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By
72	hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock:
73	
74	```bash
75	uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package           # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional
76	ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # prints a simulator api_key
77	export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY=<the api_key>
78	```
79	
80	Every call sends `X-API-Key: <key>`; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a
81	fresh `X-Move-Id` (any unique string - the same id again returns the same answer). In Postman:
82	those headers, the body as raw JSON.
83	
84	```bash
85	# 1. the cases: case:S01 has one supplier, sup:70270, and the negotiable fields unit_price, payment_days
86	curl -s "$SIM/v1/cases?set=practice" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
87	
88	# 2. open a session: the reply carries session_id (sim1 on a fresh simulator) and each supplier's quote e-mail
89	curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
90	  -H "X-Move-Id: open-1" -d '{"case_id": "case:S01"}'
91	
92	# 3. the supplier's opening e-mail: its term sheet (offer:70270-0) and the quote PDF to fetch
93	curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
94	
95	# 4. your e-mail with an offer: the reply is the supplier's answer (status, term_sheets, claim_results)
96	curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270/messages" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \
97	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Move-Id: msg-1" \
98	  -d '{"message": {"subject": "Adapter piece HI", "body": "Thank you for your quote. We offer 15.50 EUR at 60 days.",
99	       "term_sheets": [{"terms": {"unit_price": 15.5, "payment_days": 60}}]}}'
100	
101	# 5. read the reply in the thread, and the session state
102	curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
103	curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
104	```
105	
106	To close, send `{"message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:70270-1"}}}` (the
107	term sheet you take) or `{"message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}` to the same `messages` path;
108	the answer carries the result and score. The quote PDF: `GET $SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/attachments/att:70270-0-quote`.
109	The same calls work on the arena (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, your team's key, a practice case) - with
110	the clock running.
111	
112	## The Live Final: waves, in parallel, within the cap
113	
114	The final comes in 5 themed waves. A wave holds several hidden cases that appear when the host
115	starts it; play them all in parallel (up to 10 open sessions per key). Each wave has a hard
116	cap - **8 minutes** (the host may extend one) - and what is still open then ends without a deal.
117	Start the runner before the first wave and leave it running:
118	
119	```bash
120	uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
121	```
122	
123	It polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`, plays every case of a new wave at once (one agent per case),
124	closes each case **90 seconds before its wave's cap** (read from the wave's `seconds_left`, so an
125	extension counts) - earlier if a round in that case took longer
126	(`play.closing_move`: the cheapest standing term
127	sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats your alternative, else walk away) and stops after the
128	fifth wave has closed. If it crashes, start it again: it picks up the sessions it had started.
129	In Python: `play_waves(client, new_agent)`. It reads only your own cases and sessions - during
130	the final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the screen or the event feed (`arena board`
131	is for you, not for the agent).
132	
133	A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds,
134	and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the
135	limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a
136	retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before
137	Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes.
138	
139	## Your own agent
140	
141	An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`.
142	`threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with
143	their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an
144	action that closes the case:
145	
146	```python
147	from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost
148	from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
149	from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing
150	
151	
152	class Haggler:
153	    def decide(self, case, threads):
154	        sid = live_threads(threads)[0]
155	        events = threads[sid]
156	        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)  # the supplier's standing term sheet
157	        std = standard_terms(events)  # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing
158	        if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"):
159	            return {
160	                "supplier_id": sid,
161	                "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
162	            }
163	        ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97})
164	        print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask))
165	        return {
166	            "supplier_id": sid,
167	            "message": {
168	                "subject": case["title"],
169	                "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?",
170	                "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}],
171	            },
172	        }
173	
174	
175	print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler()))
176	```
177	
178	| Module | What |
179	|---|---|
180	| `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` |
181	| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) |
182	| `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion |
183	| `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms |
184	| `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases |
185	| `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline |
186	| `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts |
187	| `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) |
188	| `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below |
189	
190	The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
191	Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
192	one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
193	documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
194	questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
195	alternative.
196	
197	**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
198	deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
199	price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:
200	
201	```python
202	supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
203	total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
204	```
205	
206	## Worked example: cite an index (case P01)
207	
208	Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the
209	data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access):
210	
211	```python
212	from arena_kit.data import DataPackage
213	
214	pkg = DataPackage("data/package")
215	# 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate:
216	pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'")
217	# -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32
218	# 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year.
219	rows = pkg.query(
220	    "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month"
221	)
222	# 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart,
223	#    ending within the last 12 months of the data.
224	a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
225	change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
226	# 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs.
227	print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).")
228	# -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08
229	#    (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
230	```
231	
232	Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure
233	matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too
234	old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far,
235	is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the
236	replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which
237	supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent.
238	
239	## Choosing a model
240	
241	`LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` uses the Anthropic SDK (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` talks
242	to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`) - OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, a local
243	Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) and many more. Or pass your own `complete(system, user) -> str`
244	to `LLMAgent`. Each message must arrive within **60 seconds** of the supplier's reply: prefer a
245	fast model or low effort, and do heavy research before you open a session. If the model fails or times out, the agent falls
246	back to the naive move instead of losing the case.
247	
248	## Offline: arena-sim, the contract simulator
249	
250	```bash
251	uv run arena-sim serve --data /path/to/data/package   # http://127.0.0.1:8000, event code "sim"
252	ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # a simulator key
253	```
254	
255	`arena register` exists for the simulator only: it hands out its own keys, which work nowhere
256	else. The arena's key comes from `/apply` (step 1).
257	
258	`arena-sim` speaks the arena's public API exactly - paths, fields, statuses, error codes, limits,
259	the 60-second rule, quote PDFs and cost-breakdown XLSX files in the arena's format, RFQs with
260	parallel threads, leaderboard and replay JSON - with three example cases (`case:S01`-`S03`). Point
261	your agent at it to get the plumbing right without a network or a rate limit to worry about.
262	`--no-clock` switches the 60-second rule off for trying it by hand (above); without it the clock
263	runs, as on the arena. The first line it prints says which.
264	
265	Its supplier is a deliberately plain script and **not** how the arena's suppliers behave: it opens
266	10 % above your current price, concedes a fixed 2 % per term sheet down to 90 %, agrees when you
267	meet its price, sends a final offer from round 5 and walks if you push after that; cited data is

269	themselves** - practise against them in the hosted arena and its sandbox (`--set sandbox`). We
270	don't hand out our suppliers: for a local opponent, build your own supplier simulator from the
271	public data - how would a foundry owner with a full order book answer your e-mail?
272	`starter-kit/Dockerfile` runs the simulator as a container. `uv run pytest` runs the kit's contract
273	tests against it; set `ARENA_TEST_URL` and `ARENA_TEST_KEY` to run them against a hosted arena too.
274	
275	## MCP server over the data
276	
277	A local, read-only MCP server (stdio) lets an MCP-capable agent or chat client explore the data
278	package itself. Six tools: `list_tables`, `query` (SELECT only, max 200 rows), `lookup` (the fact
279	behind a citable ID), `list_ids` (e.g. every month of one index series), `read_document`,

# Hollerau Pumpenwerke - procurement data package v1.0.0

You are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, a fictional pump maker (start with
`company.md`). Everything is as of **2026-09-30**. Company data is synthetic; market series are real
open data (`ATTRIBUTION.md`). All company names are fictional; any match with a real company is
coincidental.

## Files
- `data/*.csv` - the master copy (UTF-8, comma, ISO dates, dot decimals); schema in `datapackage.json`.
- `world.sqlite` - the same tables in one SQLite file, generated from the CSVs.
- `facts.json` - every ID you can cite in a claim, with the values the arena checks.
- Prices are per `price_unit` (1, 100 or 1,000 pieces, kg or m), as the ERP states them; cases
  negotiate in the same unit.
- `company.md`, `SCORECARD.md`, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, `ATTRIBUTION.md`; contract texts in `contracts/`,
  letters, e-mails and notes in `correspondence/`.

## IDs
`<type>:<id>[@period]`, unique across the package, in the first column of each table: `sup:70110`,
`part:310010`, `po:4500010001-10`, `gr:`, `inv:`, `qn:`, `ctr:4600070110` (clause `ctr:4600070110#3.1`),
`quote:`, `rfq:`, `fc:310010@2026-09`, `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `cost:310010`,
`news:`, `doc:`.

## Tables
| Table | Rows | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `suppliers` | 447 | Vendor master: the detailed suppliers (`detail = full`) and the long tail (`spend only`). |
| `supplier_intel` | 46 | Public face of each detailed supplier: register facts, filed turnover, credit index, audit. |
| `parts` | 60 | Material master of the detailed parts. |
| `sourcing` | 90 | Source list: approved suppliers per part, quota, tooling owner. |
| `price_conditions` | 339 | Price history per part and supplier (price per `price_unit`), with the event behind it. |
| `negotiation_history` | 300 | Past price events: renewals with asked and settled change. |
| `contracts` | 46 | Framework agreements (text in `contracts/`). |
| `contract_clauses` | 280 | Clauses of the framework agreements, incl. index clauses (`ctr:<no>#<clause>`). |
| `po_lines` | 5400 | Purchase order lines: requested and first confirmed date, price per `price_unit`. |
| `goods_receipts` | 5580 | Goods receipts per PO line (posting date, quantity). |
| `invoices` | 5578 | Supplier invoices with due and payment dates, cash discount taken. |
| `quality_notifications` | 1033 | Complaints against suppliers (QN), with 8D dates and recharged fees. |
| `scorecards` | 414 | Rolling 12-month supplier scorecards per quarter (method: `SCORECARD.md`). |
| `forecasts` | 720 | Quarterly demand forecast snapshots per part, shared with suppliers. |
| `forecast_lines` | 8640 | Monthly quantities of each forecast snapshot. |
| `rfqs` | 47 | Requests for quotation: past benchmarks, second-source quotes, open RFQs for new parts. |
| `quotes` | 108 | Supplier quotes (price per `price_unit`); missing fields as the supplier sent them. |
| `spend_cube` | 1137 | Spend per fiscal year and supplier, incl. the long tail. |
| `index_series` | 33 | Market series: source, licence, unit; derived series with their formula. |
| `index_values` | 2258 | Monthly values of the market series (`idx:<series>@<YYYY-MM>`). |
| `cost_drivers` | 166 | The category team's estimate of each part's cost drivers (index series and weight). |
| `should_cost` | 28 | Bottom-up should-cost estimates for selected parts (`cost:<part>`). |
| `news` | 39 | Press items about suppliers and markets. |
| `documents` | 208 | Letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes (text in `correspondence/`). |

## How the tables connect
```
suppliers 1-n sourcing n-1 parts          parts 1-n price_conditions n-1 suppliers
suppliers 1-1 supplier_intel, 1-n contracts 1-n contract_clauses
po_lines -> goods_receipts -> invoices;   goods_receipts 1-n quality_notifications
parts 1-n forecasts 1-n forecast_lines;   rfqs 1-n quotes;   index_series 1-n index_values
suppliers -> scorecards, spend_cube, news, documents;   parts -> cost_drivers, should_cost
```

## Example queries (SQLite)
```sql
-- spend by supplier, last fiscal year
SELECT s.name, c.spend_eur FROM spend_cube c JOIN suppliers s ON s.id = c.supplier_id
WHERE c.fiscal_year = 'FY2026' ORDER BY c.spend_eur DESC LIMIT 10;
-- price history of one part
SELECT supplier_id, valid_from, price, price_unit FROM price_conditions WHERE part_id = 'part:310010';
-- latest scorecard per supplier
SELECT supplier_id, otd_pct, ppm, colour FROM scorecards WHERE quarter = '2026Q3' ORDER BY score;
-- an index over the last year
SELECT month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-C2451' AND month >= '2025-08';
-- how late Hollerau pays a supplier
SELECT AVG(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(due_date)) FROM invoices
WHERE supplier_id = 'sup:70210' AND discount_taken = 0 AND paid_date IS NOT NULL;
```
----
# Known issues

The data is shaped like a real ERP extract, quirks included. None of these are errors to report.

1. Three delivery dates per PO line: requested, first confirmed and the goods-receipt posting date. OTD
   differs by 10-30 points depending on the reference date.
2. Goods receipts are posted on working days only (weekends, Bavarian holidays, August shutdown).
3. Partial deliveries (two receipts per line) and small over-deliveries within 5 %.
4. C-parts, some raw material and the motor cable are priced per 100 or per 1,000 units (`price_unit`);
   a PO line's value is qty x price / price_unit.
5. One supplier sits twice in the vendor master: `sup:71999` is the old record of `sup:70210` (renamed 2024).
6. A few PO lines use an outdated price (`price_note = stale_condition`): purchase price variance.
7. Index clauses are in `contract_clauses.csv` and in the contract text (`contracts/`).
8. Past quotes miss fields where the supplier left them out (`missing_fields`).
9. Invoices are paid late for some suppliers; a few cash discounts were taken after the discount period.
10. Complaints on small lots make PPM jumpy; read the rolling scorecard, not single lots.
11. PO lines with requested dates after 2026-09-30 are open orders without receipts.
12. Index series end at different months: each source publishes with its own lag (`index_series.csv`).
13. Small suppliers file no profit and loss account: `supplier_intel.csv` gives their turnover as a band.
14. Should-cost (`should_cost.csv`) assumes a German cost base and has an error of 5-15 %.
15. The spend cube holds about 400 further suppliers known only by name, category and spend.
----
# Supplier scorecard - method

Each row (`sc:<supplier>@<quarter>`) covers the rolling 12 months to the end of that quarter and is sent to
the supplier, so both sides know it.

- **otd_pct**: share of goods-receipt lines posted between 5 days before and 2 days after the
  requested date of the PO line. **otd_confirmed_pct**: the same against the supplier's first confirmed date.
  Partial deliveries count as separate lines.
- **ppm**: supplier-caused complaint quantity / received quantity x 1,000,000 (complaints by date of the QN).
- **open_8d_overdue**: supplier-caused complaints older than 60 days without a closed 8D report at quarter end.
- **score** = 0.5 x otd_pct + 0.5 x quality points - 5 x open_8d_overdue, with quality points =
  100 x max(0, 1 - ppm / 10,000).
- **class / colour**: A green >= 85, B amber 70-84.9, C red < 70.

# Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

Family-owned pump maker from Hollerau, Lower Bavaria, Germany, founded 1952, owned by the Stangl family (third generation). Revenue about
EUR 252 M, 910 employees, one plant. Fiscal year October to September.

## Products
- **HN**: HN standard water pumps (EN 733)
- **HB**: HB building-services inline pumps
- **HI**: HI industrial process pumps, stainless (ISO 5199)
- **HX**: HX high-efficiency series (start of production 2027-03)

## Purchasing
You are the purchasing team for the pump line's parts and materials (about EUR 35 M in FY2026, see
`spend_cube.csv`). The detailed data covers the 46 suppliers and 60 parts that matter most.

## Policies
- Standard payment terms: 60 days net. Cost of capital for valuing payment terms:
  8% a year.
- Approval: deals above EUR 250 k a year need the head of purchasing, above EUR 1 M the managing director.
- A-parts are dual-sourced where a qualified second source exists (`sourcing.csv`).
- Quality agreement with every series supplier: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of
  EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint, 8D report within 60 days.
- Preferred Incoterm: DAP Hollerau. Freight for EXW/FCA deliveries is booked by Hollerau.

## Should-cost
`should_cost.csv` estimates full cost without margin. For the parts of strategic and bottleneck
negotiations the category team modelled the current supplier's own plant (`supplier_id`, error about
5 %); the other rows use a German cost base with an error of 5-15 %. Rule of thumb for other countries'
full cost relative to Germany: AT and CH about 1.0-1.1, CZ, PL and HU about 0.8-0.85, TR about 0.75,
CN about 0.7.

## Category strategies
Every negotiation states its category goal (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine`); the rates of its cost C follow it.
Quality escalations are `quality_first`, capacity squeezes `secure_supply`, kits and bundles `routine`.

| Category | Strategy | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| castings | secure supply and energy-cost transparency; build Central-European second sources | stabilise |
| machined parts | leverage: competition between local job shops, bundle small parts | leverage |
| sheet metal | leverage; quality first after the 2026 base-frame issues | leverage |
| seals | bottleneck: long-term agreements, qualify second sources where approvals allow | secure_supply |
| electrical | strategic: copper and electronics clauses, multi-year frameworks | stabilise |
| C-parts | routine: fewer suppliers, kits, lower process cost | routine |
| raw material | index-based pricing, negotiate base price and extras | leverage |

## Targets for FY2027
Material cost -3 % against the index-adjusted baseline; no supplier in red for more than two quarters.

158	                alt.get("kind") in (None, "none")
159	                or not alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price")
160	                or total_cost(case, terms, std) <= total_cost(case, alt["terms"])
161	            )
162	            if sheet_id and must_haves_ok(case, terms, std) and beats:
163	                return {
164	                    "supplier_id": sid,
165	                    "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
166	                }
167	            return None
168	        if kind != "send" or moves_left(case, events) <= 0:
169	            return None
170	        sheets = []
171	        for ts in (d.get("term_sheets") or [])[:3]:
172	            t = complete_offer(case, {**terms, **ts.get("terms", ts)})
173	            if t not in sheets:
174	                sheets.append(t)
175	        offers = {standing(ev)[0] for ev in threads.values()}
176	
177	        def known(m):  # an ID the data does not have would read as a lie
178	            if m.group(0) in offers or self.fact(case, m.group(0)):
179	                return m.group(0)
180	            log.warning("dropped unknown data ID %s", m.group(0))
181	            return ""
182	
183	        body = re.sub(r"\s*\(\s*[,;\s]*\)", "", ID_RE.sub(known, str(d.get("body", ""))))
184	        body = body.strip()[:8000]
185	        subject = str(d.get("subject") or f"Re: {case['title']}")[:300]
186	        return {
187	            "supplier_id": sid,
188	            "message": {
189	                "subject": subject,
190	                "body": body,
191	                "term_sheets": [{"terms": t} for t in sheets],
192	            },
193	        }
194	
195	
196	def parse(text):
197	    """The first JSON object in the model's reply (tolerates code fences and chatter)."""
198	    match = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S)
199	    if not match:
200	        raise ValueError(f"no JSON in reply: {text[:200]}")
201	    return json.loads(match.group(0))

1	"""Play cases with an agent against the arena over HTTP - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox,
2	final) or `arena-sim`, the local contract simulator. Both speak the same API.
3	
4	An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": ..., "message": {...}}`:
5	  threads: {supplier_id: [message, ...]} - every e-mail so far, both directions, in order;
6	           supplier attachments carry their text under "text" (see `docs.read_document`).
7	  message: subject, body, up to 3 term sheets, refs - or an "action" that closes the case:
8	           {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": ...} or {"type": "walk_away"}.
9	"""
10	
11	import functools
12	import logging
13	import re
14	import threading
15	import time
16	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
17	
18	from .client import ArenaError
19	from .cost import must_haves_ok, total_cost
20	from .docs import read_document, standard_terms
21	
22	log = logging.getLogger("arena")
23	
24	ENDED = {"walked_away", "no_bid"}
25	# A message later than this after the supplier's last one counts as a timeout.
26	MOVE_LIMIT_S = 60
27	# In the Live Final, close this long before the wave's cap - or the slowest round of the case so far
28	# (your decision plus a supplier reply of up to about a minute) plus a margin, if that is longer.
29	CLOSE_BEFORE_CAP_S, ROUND_MARGIN_S = 90, 15
30	RUNNING = re.compile(r"one session per case in the final: (\S+)")
31	# Practice: the case list shows every practice case file; only those marked hosted can be played
32	# (a session on another is a 403). Without the marker every listed case counts as hosted.
33	HOSTED_FIELD = "hosted"
34	
35	
36	class RemoteTable:
37	    """The arena over HTTP: the practice arena, the final, or a hosted sandbox."""
38	
39	    def __init__(self, client, case=None):
40	        self.client, self.session_id, self.case, self.done = client, None, case, None
41	
42	    def open(self, case_id):
43	        try:
44	            r = self.client.open_session(case_id)
45	        except ArenaError as e:
46	            running = RUNNING.search(str(e.detail)) if e.status == 409 else None
47	            if not (running and self.case):
48	                raise
49	            return self.resume(running.group(1))
50	        self.session_id = r["session_id"]
51	        log.info("session %s", self.session_id)
52	        return r["case"], r["threads"]
53	
54	    def resume(self, session_id):
55	        """Pick up a final session this team already started (e.g. after a crash): every thread
56	        so far, from the arena."""
57	        self.session_id = session_id
58	        log.info("resuming session %s", session_id)
59	        state = self.client.session(session_id)
60	        if state["status"] == "ended":
61	            self.done = self.result()
62	        return self.case, {s: self.client.thread(session_id, s)["messages"] for s in state["threads"]}
63	
64	    def send(self, supplier_id, message):
65	        return self.client.send_message(self.session_id, supplier_id, message)
66	
67	    def close(self, supplier_id, message):
68	        reply = self.client.send_message(self.session_id, supplier_id, message)
69	        return reply.get("result", reply)  # the supplier's last e-mail carries the result
70	
71	    def attachment(self, attachment_id):
72	        return self.client.attachment(self.session_id, attachment_id)
73	
74	    def missed(self, supplier_id, error):
75	        """After a 409: the result if the case has ended (e.g. at a wave's cap), else what the
76	        thread now says (a timeout answer, or the reason it ended)."""
77	        state = self.client.session(self.session_id)
78	        if state.get("status") == "ended":
79	            return {"result": state.get("result") or {"deal": False, "end_reason": state.get("end_reason")}}
80	        t = self.client.thread(self.session_id, supplier_id)
81	        last = (t.get("timeouts") or [{}])[-1]
82	        sheet = [{"term_sheet_id": t["offer_id"], "terms": last.get("terms", {})}]
83	        return {
84	            "from": "arena",
85	            "status": "walked_away" if t["closed"] else t["status"],
86	            "term_sheets": [] if t["closed"] else sheet,
87	            "body": f"({error.detail})",
88	            "missing_fields": last.get("missing_fields", []),
89	            "attachments": [],
90	        }
91	
92	    def result(self):
93	        state = self.client.session(self.session_id)
94	        return state.get("result") or {"deal": False, "end_reason": state.get("end_reason"), **state}
95	
96	
97	def latest(events):
98	    """The supplier's latest message in a thread."""
99	    return next(m for m in reversed(events) if m.get("from") != "buyer")
100	
101	
102	def standing(events):
103	    """(term_sheet_id, terms) of the supplier's standing term sheet, or (None, {})."""
104	    sheets = latest(events).get("term_sheets") or []
105	    return (sheets[0]["term_sheet_id"], sheets[0]["terms"]) if sheets else (None, {})
106	
107	
108	def live_threads(threads):
109	    """Suppliers whose thread has not ended."""
110	    return [sid for sid, ev in threads.items() if latest(ev).get("status") not in ENDED]
111	
112	
113	def moves_left(case, events):
114	    """Messages you may still send in this thread (the round limit counts each of them)."""
115	    return case.get("round_limit", 10) - sum(m.get("from") == "buyer" for m in events)
116	
117	
118	def fetch_documents(table, message):
119	    """Download every attachment of a supplier message and add its text."""
120	    for att in message.get("attachments") or []:
121	        if att.get("attachment_id") and "text" not in att:
122	            att["text"] = read_document(att["name"], table.attachment(att["attachment_id"]))
123	    return message
124	
125	
126	def closing_move(case, threads):
127	    """Accept the cheapest standing term sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative
128	    (C with each supplier's standard terms), else walk away - what to do when time runs out."""
129	    alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
130	    c_alt = total_cost(case, alt["terms"]) if alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") else float("inf")
131	    best = None
132	    for sid in live_threads(threads):
133	        sheet_id, terms = standing(threads[sid])
134	        std = standard_terms(threads[sid])
135	        if sheet_id and must_haves_ok(case, terms, std) and (c := total_cost(case, terms, std)) < c_alt:
136	            best = min(best or (c, sid, sheet_id), (c, sid, sheet_id))
137	    if best is None:
138	        return {"supplier_id": live_threads(threads)[0], "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
139	    return {"supplier_id": best[1], "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": best[2]}}}
140	
141	
142	def play(table, case_id, agent, deadline=None):
143	    """Play one case to its end. `deadline` (time.time(), or a function returning it): a Live Final
144	    wave's cap - shortly before it, `closing_move` closes the case so it does not end without a deal."""
145	    case, threads = table.open(case_id)
146	    if getattr(table, "done", None):  # resumed a case that had already ended
147	        return table.done
148	    for events in threads.values():
149	        for m in events:
150	            fetch_documents(table, m)
151	    slowest = 0.0  # the longest round so far: decision + the supplier's reply
152	    while live_threads(threads):
153	        t0 = time.monotonic()
154	        cap = deadline() if callable(deadline) else deadline
155	        if cap and time.time() > cap - max(CLOSE_BEFORE_CAP_S, slowest + ROUND_MARGIN_S):
156	            log.info("%s: the wave's cap is near - closing", case_id)
157	            decision = closing_move(case, threads)
158	        else:
159	            decision = agent.decide(case, threads)
160	        if (took := time.monotonic() - t0) > MOVE_LIMIT_S * 0.75:
161	            log.warning("decision took %.1fs - the limit is %ss per message", took, MOVE_LIMIT_S)
162	        sid, msg = decision["supplier_id"], decision["message"]
163	        try:
164	            if msg.get("action"):
165	                log.info("%s %s", sid, msg["action"])
166	                return table.close(sid, msg)
167	            reply = table.send(sid, msg)
168	        except ArenaError as e:
169	            if e.status != 409:
170	                raise
171	            log.info("%s: %s", sid, e.detail)
172	            reply = table.missed(sid, e)  # e.g. late, or the thread or the case has ended
173	            if msg.get("action") and "result" not in reply:  # the case goes on: decide again
174	                threads[sid].append(fetch_documents(table, reply))
175	                continue
176	        if "result" in reply:  # the reply ended the case, e.g. the last supplier walked away
177	            return reply["result"]
178	        threads[sid] += [{**msg, "from": "buyer"}, fetch_documents(table, reply)]
179	        slowest = max(slowest, time.monotonic() - t0)
180	        log.info("%s %s %s", sid, reply.get("status"), standing(threads[sid])[1])
181	    return table.result()
182	
183	
184	def hosted(cases):
185	    """The cases you can play: those marked hosted, or all of them if the list has no marker."""
186	    if any(HOSTED_FIELD in c for c in cases):
187	        return [c for c in cases if c.get(HOSTED_FIELD)]
188	    return cases
189	
190	
191	def quota_used_up(error):
192	    """The practice quota's 429 ("practice limit: …"): retrying does not help before it resets."""
193	    return isinstance(error, ArenaError) and error.status == 429 and str(error.detail).startswith("practice limit")
194	
195	
196	def play_all(new_table, case_ids, new_agent, parallel=8):
197	    """Play many cases at once (e.g. every practice case). `new_table()` and `new_agent()` give
198	    each case its own table and agent. Once the practice quota is used up, no further case starts.
199	    Returns {case_id: result or the exception that stopped it}."""
200	    used_up = threading.Event()
201	
202	    def one(case_id):
203	        if used_up.is_set():
204	            return case_id, ArenaError(429, "not started: the practice quota is used up")
205	        try:
206	            return case_id, play(new_table(), case_id, new_agent())
207	        except ArenaError as e:
208	            if quota_used_up(e):
209	                used_up.set()
210	                log.warning("practice quota used up: %s", e.detail)
211	            elif e.status == 403:
212	                log.warning("%s: %s", case_id, e.detail)  # e.g. not hosted for practice
213	            else:
214	                log.exception("%s failed", case_id)
215	            return case_id, e
216	        except Exception as e:  # one broken case must not stop the others
217	            log.exception("%s failed", case_id)
218	            return case_id, e
219	
220	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel) as pool:
221	        return dict(pool.map(one, case_ids))
222	
223	
224	def play_waves(client, new_agent, waves=5, parallel=10, poll=5.0):
225	    """The Live Final: wait for each wave, play its cases in parallel within the wave's cap, wait
226	    for the next. Keep it running from before the first wave until the last has closed; it returns
227	    after `waves` waves have closed and every case has finished: {case_id: result or exception}."""
228	    started, closed, caps = {}, set(), {}  # caps: wave -> its cap as time.time()
229	
230	    def one(case, deadline):
231	        try:
232	            return play(RemoteTable(client, case), case["case_id"], new_agent(), deadline)
233	        except Exception as e:  # one broken case must not stop the others
234	            log.exception("%s failed", case["case_id"])
235	            return e
236	
237	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel) as pool:
238	        while len(closed) < waves or not all(f.done() for f in started.values()):
239	            try:
240	                cases = client.cases("final")
241	            except ArenaError as e:
242	                if e.status != 403:  # 403: no wave has started yet
243	                    raise
244	                cases = []
245	            for case in cases:
246	                if not case.get("open"):
247	                    closed.add(case["wave"])
248	                    continue
249	                if case.get("seconds_left") is not None:  # each wave has its own cap; follow an extension
250	                    caps[case["wave"]] = time.time() + case["seconds_left"]
251	                if case["case_id"] not in started and case.get("seconds_left"):
252	                    if case["wave"] not in {c["wave"] for c in cases if c["case_id"] in started}:
253	                        log.warning("wave %s started: %s", case["wave"], case.get("theme"))
254	                    started[case["case_id"]] = pool.submit(one, case, functools.partial(caps.get, case["wave"]))
255	            time.sleep(poll)
256	    return {case_id: f.result() for case_id, f in started.items()}
257

content.text:
# Update Config Skill

Modify Claude Code configuration by updating settings.json files.

## When Hooks Are Required (Not Memory)

If the user wants something to happen automatically in response to an EVENT, they need a **hook** configured in settings.json. Memory/preferences cannot trigger automated actions.

**These require hooks:**
- "Before compacting, ask me what to preserve" → PreCompact hook
- "After writing files, run prettier" → PostToolUse hook with Write|Edit matcher
- "When I run bash commands, log them" → PreToolUse hook with Bash matcher
- "Always run tests after code changes" → PostToolUse hook

**Hook events:** PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, Notification, SessionStart

## CRITICAL: Read Before Write

**Always read the existing settings file before making changes.** Merge new settings with existing ones - never replace the entire file.

## CRITICAL: Use AskUserQuestion for Ambiguity

When the user's request is ambiguous, use AskUserQuestion to clarify:
- Which settings file to modify (user/project/local)
- Whether to add to existing arrays or replace them
- Specific values when multiple options exist

## Decision: /config command vs Direct Edit

**Suggest the `/config` slash command** for these simple settings:
- `theme`, `editorMode`, `verbose`, `model`
- `language`, `alwaysThinkingEnabled`
- `permissions.defaultMode`

**Edit settings.json directly** for:
- Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.)
- Complex permission rules (allow/deny arrays)
- Environment variables
- MCP server configuration
- Plugin configuration

## Workflow

1. **Clarify intent** - Ask if the request is ambiguous
2. **Read existing file** - Use Read tool on the target settings file
3. **Merge carefully** - Preserve existing settings, especially arrays
4. **Edit file** - Use Edit tool (if file doesn't exist, ask user to create it first)
5. **Confirm** - Tell user what was changed

## Merging Arrays (Important!)

When adding to permission arrays or hook arrays, **merge with existing**, don't replace:

**WRONG** (replaces existing permissions):
```json
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(npm *)"] } }
```

**RIGHT** (preserves existing + adds new):
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git *)",      // existing
      "Edit(.claude)",    // existing
      "Bash(npm *)"       // new
    ]
  }
}
```

## Settings File Locations

Choose the appropriate file based on scope:

| File | Scope | Git | Use For |
|------|-------|-----|---------|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Global | N/A | Personal preferences for all projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Project | Commit | Team-wide hooks, permissions, plugins |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project | Gitignore | Personal overrides for this project |

Settings load in order: user → project → local (later overrides earlier).

## Settings Schema Reference

### Permissions
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(npm *)", "Edit(.claude)", "Read"],
    "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"],
    "ask": ["Edit(//etc/*)"],
    "defaultMode": "default" | "plan" | "acceptEdits" | "dontAsk",
    "additionalDirectories": ["/extra/dir"]
  }
}
```

**Permission Rule Syntax:**
- Exact match: `"Bash(npm run test)"`
- Prefix wildcard: `"Bash(git *)"` - matches `git`, `git status`, `git commit`, etc.
- Tool only: `"Read"` - allows all Read operations
- File paths: `"Edit(src/**)"` - path rules in `permissions` use `Edit(path)` for every file-writing tool (Write, Edit, NotebookEdit) and `Read(path)` for reads. `Write(path)`, `NotebookEdit(path)` and `Glob(path)` rules are not matched by file permission checks. Bare tool names (`"Write"`), deny/ask `Tool(param:value)` rules and hook `if` conditions still use each tool's own name

### Environment Variables
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DEBUG": "true",
    "MY_API_KEY": "value"
  }
}
```

### Model & Agent
```json
{
  "model": "sonnet",  // or "fable", "opus", "haiku", full model ID
  "agent": "agent-name",
  "alwaysThinkingEnabled": true
}
```

### Attribution (Commits & PRs)
```json
{
  "attribution": {
    "commit": "Custom commit trailer text",
    "pr": "Custom PR description text"
  }
}
```
Set `commit` or `pr` to empty string `""` to hide that attribution. To hide all of it, set both to `""` and also set `"sessionUrl": false`. Write this object form, not `"attribution": false`: older Claude Code versions reject true or false here and then skip the whole settings file.

### MCP Server Management
```json
{
  "enableAllProjectMcpServers": true,
  "enabledMcpjsonServers": ["server1", "server2"],
  "disabledMcpjsonServers": ["blocked-server"]
}
```

### Plugins
```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "formatter@anthropic-tools": true
  }
}
```
Plugin syntax: `plugin-name@source` where source is `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-plugins-official`, or `builtin`.

### Other Settings
- `language`: Preferred response language (e.g., "japanese")
- `cleanupPeriodDays`: Days to keep transcripts before automatic cleanup (default: 30; minimum 1)
- `respectGitignore`: Whether to respect .gitignore (default: true)
- `spinnerTipsEnabled`: Show tips in spinner
- `timeFormat`: Clock format for times shown in the UI: "auto" (default), "12-hour", "24-hour", "24-hour-utc", or a strftime pattern such as "%H:%M"
- `timeZone`: IANA time zone for times shown in the UI, e.g. "UTC" (default: system time zone)
- `spinnerVerbs`: Customize spinner verbs (`{ "mode": "append" | "replace", "verbs": [...] }`)
- `spinnerTipsOverride`: Override spinner tips (`{ "excludeDefault": true, "tips": ["Custom tip"] }`)
- `syntaxHighlightingDisabled`: Disable diff highlighting


## Hooks Configuration

Hooks run commands at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.

### Hook Structure
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "EVENT_NAME": [
      {
        "matcher": "ToolName|OtherTool",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "your-command-here",
            "timeout": 60,
            "statusMessage": "Running..."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Hook Events

| Event | Matcher | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| PermissionRequest | Tool name | Run before permission prompt |
| PreToolUse | Tool name | Run before tool, can block |
| PostToolUse | Tool name | Run after successful tool |
| PostToolUseFailure | Tool name | Run after tool fails |
| Notification | Notification type | Run on notifications |
| Stop | - | Run when Claude stops (including clear, resume, compact) |
| PreCompact | "manual"/"auto" | Before compaction |
| PostCompact | "manual"/"auto" | After compaction (receives summary) |
| UserPromptSubmit | - | When user submits |
| SessionStart | - | When session starts |

**Common tool matchers:** `Bash`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`

### Hook Types

**1. Command Hook** - Runs a shell command:
```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "prettier --write $FILE", "timeout": 30 }
```

**2. Prompt Hook** - Evaluates a condition with LLM:
```json
{ "type": "prompt", "prompt": "Is this safe? $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

**3. Agent Hook** - Runs an agent with tools:
```json
{ "type": "agent", "prompt": "Verify tests pass: $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

### Hook Input (stdin JSON)
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "tool_name": "Write",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt", "content": "..." },
  "tool_response": { "success": true }  // PostToolUse only
}
```

### Hook JSON Output

Hooks can return JSON to control behavior:

```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Warning shown to user in UI",
  "continue": false,
  "stopReason": "Message shown when blocking",
  "suppressOutput": false,
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Explanation for decision",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
    "additionalContext": "Context injected back to model"
  }
}
```

**Fields:**
- `systemMessage` - Display a message to the user (all hooks)
- `continue` - Set to `false` to block/stop (default: true)
- `stopReason` - Message shown when `continue` is false
- `suppressOutput` - Hide stdout from transcript (default: false)
- `decision` - "block" for PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks (deprecated for PreToolUse, use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision instead)
- `reason` - Explanation for decision
- `hookSpecificOutput` - Event-specific output (must include `hookEventName`):
  - `additionalContext` - Text injected into model context
  - `permissionDecision` - "allow", "deny", or "ask" (PreToolUse only)
  - `permissionDecisionReason` - Reason for the permission decision (PreToolUse only)
  - `updatedInput` - Modified tool input (PreToolUse only)

### Common Patterns

**Auto-format after writes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Log all bash commands:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.command' >> ~/.claude/bash-log.txt"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Stop hook that displays message to user:**

Command must output JSON with `systemMessage` field:
```bash
# Example command that outputs: {"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}
echo '{"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}'
```

**Run tests after code changes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath' | grep -E '\\.(ts|js)$' && npm test || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```


## Constructing a Hook (with verification)

Given an event, matcher, target file, and desired behavior, follow this flow. Each step catches a different failure class — a hook that silently does nothing is worse than no hook.

1. **Dedup check.** Read the target file. If a hook already exists on the same event+matcher, show the existing command and ask: keep it, replace it, or add alongside.

2. **Construct the command for THIS project — don't assume.** The hook receives JSON on stdin. Build a command that:
   - Extracts any needed payload safely — use `jq -r` into a quoted variable or `{ read -r f; ... "$f"; }`, NOT unquoted `| xargs` (splits on spaces)
   - Invokes the underlying tool the way this project runs it (npx/bunx/yarn/pnpm? Makefile target? globally-installed?)
   - Skips inputs the tool doesn't handle (formatters often have `--ignore-unknown`; if not, guard by extension)
   - Stays RAW for now — no `|| true`, no stderr suppression. You'll wrap it after the pipe-test passes.

3. **Pipe-test the raw command.** Synthesize the stdin payload the hook will receive and pipe it directly:
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Write|Edit`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<a real file from this repo>"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Bash`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart`: most commands don't read stdin, so `echo '{}' | <cmd>` suffices

   Check exit code AND side effect (file actually formatted, test actually ran). If it fails you get a real error — fix (wrong package manager? tool not installed? jq path wrong?) and retest. Once it works, wrap with `2>/dev/null || true` (unless the user wants a blocking check).

4. **Write the JSON.** Merge into the target file (schema shape in the "Hook Structure" section above). If this creates `.claude/settings.local.json` for the first time, add it to .gitignore — the Write tool doesn't auto-gitignore it.

5. **Validate syntax + schema in one shot:**

   `jq -e '.hooks.<event>[] | select(.matcher == "<matcher>") | .hooks[] | select(.type == "command") | .command' <target-file>`

   Exit 0 + prints your command = correct. Exit 4 = matcher doesn't match. Exit 5 = malformed JSON or wrong nesting. A broken settings.json silently disables ALL settings from that file — fix any pre-existing malformation too.

6. **Prove the hook fires** — only for `Pre|PostToolUse` on a matcher you can trigger in-turn (`Write|Edit` via Edit, `Bash` via Bash). `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart` fire outside this turn — skip to step 7.

   For a **formatter** on `PostToolUse`/`Write|Edit`: introduce a detectable violation via Edit (two consecutive blank lines, bad indentation, missing semicolon — something this formatter corrects; NOT trailing whitespace, Edit strips that before writing), re-read, confirm the hook **fixed** it. For **anything else**: temporarily prefix the command in settings.json with `echo "$(date) hook fired" >> /tmp/claude-hook-check.txt; `, trigger the matching tool (Edit for `Write|Edit`, a harmless `true` for `Bash`), read the sentinel file.

   **Always clean up** — revert the violation, strip the sentinel prefix — whether the proof passed or failed.

   **If proof fails but pipe-test passed and `jq -e` passed**: the settings watcher isn't watching `.claude/` — it only watches directories that had a settings file when this session started. The hook is written correctly. Tell the user to start a new session so the new settings load. You can't do this yourself.

7. **Handoff.** Tell the user the hook is live (or needs a new session per the watcher caveat), and that they can review, edit, or disable it later in the settings file you wrote. The UI only shows "Ran N hooks" if a hook errors or is slow — silent success is invisible by design.


## Example Workflows

### Adding a Hook

User: "Format my code after Claude writes it"

1. **Clarify**: Which formatter? (prettier, gofmt, etc.)
2. **Read**: `.claude/settings.json` (or create if missing)
3. **Merge**: Add to existing hooks, don't replace
4. **Result**:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Adding Permissions

User: "Allow npm commands without prompting"

1. **Read**: Existing permissions
2. **Merge**: Add `Bash(npm *)` to allow array
3. **Result**: Combined with existing allows

### Environment Variables

User: "Set DEBUG=true"

1. **Decide**: User settings (global) or project settings?
2. **Read**: Target file
3. **Merge**: Add to env object
```json
{ "env": { "DEBUG": "true" } }
```

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. **Replacing instead of merging** - Always preserve existing settings
2. **Wrong file** - Ask user if scope is unclear
3. **Invalid JSON** - Validate syntax after changes
4. **Forgetting to read first** - Always read before write

## Troubleshooting Hooks

If a hook isn't running:
1. **Check the settings file** - Read ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json
2. **Verify JSON syntax** - Invalid JSON silently fails
3. **Check the matcher** - Does it match the tool name? (e.g., "Bash", "Write", "Edit")
4. **Check hook type** - Is it "command", "prompt", or "agent"?
5. **Test the command** - Run the hook command manually to see if it works
6. **Use --debug** - Run `claude --debug` to see hook execution logs

Affects every spend figure Claude Code reports — /cost, the status line, the SDK total_cost_usd, --max-budget-usd, and the OpenTelemetry cost metric and events — which remain USD estimates, not an invoice (the per-Mtok price labels in /model stay at list). \"overrides\" maps a model ID to its USD-per-million-token rates (input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite — all four required, each 0 to 10000; cacheWrite prices both 5-minute and 1-hour cache writes). A matching row is charged exactly as written; fast-mode and US-data-residency surcharges are not added on top. A key Claude Code itself uses for a built-in model — its ID such as \"claude-sonnet-4-6\", or its first-party, Bedrock (any or no region prefix), Vertex or Foundry ID — covers every dated and provider form of that model; any other key — a gateway model alias, or a spelling Claude Code does not itself use — matches that model ID only (case-insensitive), and such an exact match wins over a built-in row. On Bedrock an application inference profile is matched by its backing model.
